subject.title: fix(whatsapp): add chunk-idle timeout to inbound media download

question: Should WhatsApp inbound media adopt the fixed 30-second per-chunk cutoff based on the local production-boundary proof, or should the cutoff or live-proof requirement change before merge?
rationale: Code inspection can establish correctness of the timeout mechanism, but only the WhatsApp owners can accept the production tradeoff between releasing indefinitely stalled dispatch and aborting unusually slow legitimate downloads.

options.title: Accept the 30-second cutoff
options.body: Land after exact-head checks because the value follows existing channel precedent and the loopback proof covers timeout, teardown, and normal transfer.

options.title: Retune the fixed cutoff
options.body: Choose a WhatsApp-specific duration and update the focused timing assertions before merge.

options.title: Require live WhatsApp recovery proof
options.body: Pause until a real session demonstrates a stalled media message timing out without blocking a subsequent inbound message.

recommendation.title: Accept the 30-second cutoff
recommendation.body: Land after exact-head checks because the value follows existing channel precedent and the loopback proof covers timeout, teardown, and normal transfer.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history shows the strongest ownership of WhatsApp inbound lifecycle and dispatch boundaries.
